limitations: 50ms sampling can miss stalls within an unsampled interval; every final tail is incomplete, overdue pending callback is a lower bound, and zero observed lateness is not zero delay proof.

Page guard entries count admission checks without per-operation clock reads; terminal deadline/closed checks do not enter the guard. Monotonic snapshots occur at safe boundaries, so the largest observed unchecked interval is conservative, not exact, and multiple-check spans retain their check count.
Scheduling lateness includes timer scheduling and process descheduling, not its cause or per-request CPU utilization.
Native service spans and phase spans overlap; they cannot be subtracted to infer active execution or provider CPU.
Date.now remains authoritative for the 1000ms ledger; wall clock changes can shorten or extend its monotonic lifetime.
Small controlled non-reproduction and passing forced deadline assertions do not repair or waive the alpha.23 historical failures.
